chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari. He said: I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) say:

My God! Your power is apparent, yet You have not appeared in any form. So they became ignorant of You and tried to measure You, while the true measure is other than how they describe You. And indeed I dissociate, O my God, from those who seek You through anthropomorphism. There is nothing like unto You. My God, they shall never comprehend You. The apparent blessings they have from You would be their indicator toward You, had they recognized You. And in Your creation, O my God, there is ample evidence that precludes them from grasping You through similitude, yet they equated You with Your creation, and thence they did not recognize You. They took some of Your signs as a lord, and by that they described You. You are exalted, my Lord, above what the anthropomorphists attribute to You.

key_terms.المشبهون: Al-Mushabbihun: the anthropomorphists, those who liken God to His creation
key_terms.تشبيه: Tashbih: anthropomorphism, likening God to creation
key_terms.مندوحة: Manduhah: ample scope, indicating God's creation is far removed from being used as similitude for Him

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about anthropomorphism and God's transcendence?
ai.summary: This is a supplication by Imam al-Rida (AS) on divine transcendence (tanzih), recorded by al-Shaykh al-Saduq. The Imam emphatically rejects anthropomorphism (tashbih) and affirms that God's power is manifest without form. He echoes the Quranic verse "There is nothing like unto Him" (42:11), which was a central proof-text in classical Islamic debates about divine attributes. The original audience, gathered at a scholarly assembly in 368 AH, would have understood this as a reaffirmation of the Imamic theological position against the Mushabbihah (anthropomorphists).

and they tried to measure You

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from Abi Hisham al-Ja`fari. He said: I heard `Ali b. Musa al-Rida (as) say:

My God! Your power is apparent, even though You do not have a form. So, they become ignorant of You and they [try to] measure You, while the [true] measure is other than how they describe You. I dissociate, My God, from those who seek You by alikeness (tashbih). There is none like unto You. My God! They cannot comprehend You. If they [wanted to] recognize You, their indicator would be the apparent of Your blessings with them. Your creation, My Lord, is far removed from being used [as a similitude] to understanding You, but they compare You to Your creation, and thusly they do not recognize You. They have taken Your signs as a lord, and by that they describe You. You are exalted, my Lord, over what those who liken describe You by.
